key_insight: The paper shows that ten-class MNIST can run end-to-end on IBM’s 127-qubit Eagle chip using a train-offline, infer-on-hardware workflow with quantum multi-programming for faster parallel inference.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical NISQ deployment pattern: avoid costly on-device training, use the hardware mainly for inference, and improve throughput by packing multiple circuits onto one processor.
method: Two-phase training: classical gradient-based optimization for the encoder/readout, then gradient-free optimization for quantum parameters.
Quantum Multi-Programming: place multiple circuit copies on one device to run several inferences in parallel.
Compare hardware fine-tuning versus simulator training, and benchmark the quantum model against a classical network of matched capacity.
evidence_signal: In their evaluation, on-hardware fine-tuning did not produce measurable accuracy gains, and the quantum model showed no per-parameter accuracy advantage over a matched classical baseline.
watch_item: The approach is still limited by NISQ noise and scale, so performance gains depend on inference-only use and may not generalize to larger or more complex datasets.
paper_title: Image Classification on IBM Quantum Computers
